new_hypotheses.name: mlb_opener_strategy_total_over
new_hypotheses.thesis: When an MLB team deploys an opener (reliever starting, typically throwing 1-2 innings before a bulk pitcher), F5 overs are mispriced because oddsmakers set the line based on the scheduled bulk pitcher's ERA rather than the 2-3 relievers who actually face the first 15+ batters. Opener strategies correlate with bullpen fatigue and run-scoring volatility in innings 2-4.

new_hypotheses.name: nhl_goalie_pull_strategy_3p_total
new_hypotheses.thesis: Teams trailing by 1 in the 3rd period pull their goalie with 2-3 minutes remaining, creating a 6v5 that generates ~2.5x the shot rate but also allows empty-net goals. Oddsmakers price live 3rd period totals on base scoring rate, not on pull probability which is near-certain for 1-goal deficits after 15:00 of the 3rd. The over on 3rd period totals when the score differential is exactly 1 should be systematically underpriced.

new_hypotheses.name: mlb_catcher_framing_f5_total
new_hypotheses.thesis: Elite pitch-framing catchers (top-10 by framing runs above average) expand the effective strike zone by 0.5-1.0 inches, generating 2-4 extra called strikes per game. When a top-10 framing catcher faces a bottom-10 framing catcher, the differential in called strike rate creates a measurable F5 scoring asymmetry that soft books do not price because catcher framing data is not in standard oddsmaking models.

new_hypotheses.name: nhl_schedule_trap_regulation_win
new_hypotheses.thesis: When a contending team (top-8 in conference) plays a non-contender the night BEFORE a divisional rival matchup, the contender's regulation win probability drops ~8-12% due to subconscious energy conservation. Oddsmakers price the H2H line but do NOT adjust the regulation win market (-1.5 puck line), creating mispricing in the exact-score/regulation-win alt spread.
